head: Before
After
rows: The writer says the river argues. This is personification.

The river is 'arguing' beneath the bridge, so the water seems restless and angry; the verb makes the bridge precious because it holds two quarrelling sides together, and the writer wants us to value what keeps people connected.

model.title: How does the writer present the bridge as precious?

parts.text: Before: 'The writer says the river argues. This is personification.'

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: The writer presents the bridge as alive with history: the river is 'arguing with the arches', a personification that suggests an old, familiar quarrel, so destroying the bridge would end a conversation four hundred years long.
